jobs.jd: PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns. Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients. Role Overview We are seeking a Surveillance Data Scientist to help build and scale surveillance capabilities across private asset-backed finance. Sitting at the intersection of investments, data and technology, the role will develop analytical tools and data infrastructure that enable Portfolio Managers, Asset Management and Risk to monitor performance, compare realized outcomes with underwriting assumptions and identify emerging risks and opportunities. Responsibilities Design and build analytical tools for private asset-backed investments, including loan-level performance aggregators, return calculators, benchmarking tools and exception identification. Build and automate data flows with Technology to support accurate exposure, collateral, cash-flow and performance monitoring. Develop consistent surveillance across standardized asset types such as consumer loans, student loans and auto finance, and extend capabilities over time to mortgage whole loans and other private asset classes. Reconcile realized performance against underwriting assumptions, identify material variances and help translate findings into actionable insights for Portfolio Managers, Asset Management and Risk. Partner with public- and private-side Technology teams to develop reusable tools and APIs for investment and analytical platforms. Work directly with Portfolio Managers, Asset Management, Risk and quantitative modelers to identify gaps in investment performance analysis, assumptions and models. Produce clear surveillance reporting and, over time, targeted sector research to identify performance trends and relative-value opportunities. Requirements Master's degree in Financial Engineering, quantitative finance, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative discipline. Strong quantitative skills and a solid understanding of structured credit and asset-backed investments; experience with private credit or asset-backed finance is strongly preferred. Hands-on working knowledge of Python and SQL, with the ability to query data, develop analytical tools and automate repeatable processes. Experience working with loan-level, collateral, cash-flow or investment-performance data and translating analysis into practical investment insights. Ability to work independently in an evolving environment, shape solutions from ambiguous requirements and partner effectively across investment, risk and technology teams. Strong written and verbal communication. PIMCO follows a total compensation approach when rewarding employees which includes a base salary and a discretionary bonus. Base salary is the fixed component of compensation that is determined by core job responsibilities, relevant experience, internal level, and market factors. The discretionary bonus is used to award performance and therefore is determined by company, business, team, and individual performance. jobs.jd: Employee Applicant Privacy Notice Who we are: Shape a brighter financial future with us. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world. The Role The Operations Data Science team is looking for a Data Scientist to drive data-informed decision-making across our Member Experience organization. This role will partner closely with Operations, Contact Center, Product, and Engineering teams to identify opportunities to improve the end-to-end member experience, optimize operational processes, and help the organization achieve its goal of delivering an exceptional member experience (NPS 70). You will leverage experimentation, statistical analysis, and data-driven insights to understand the drivers of member satisfaction and identify opportunities to improve the member journey across various products, frontline agent tools and workflows, and manual review processes. The ideal candidate combines strong technical and analytical skills with business acumen and the ability to translate complex analyses into actionable recommendations that drive meaningful operational and member experience improvements. What you’ll do: Define and measure operational and member experience KPIs, including NPS, CSAT, resolution rates, and member effort. Design and analyze A/B tests and quasi-experiments to measure the impact of operational improvements and agent tooling. Conduct root cause and deep-dive analyses to identify member friction, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement. Partner with Operations Product and Teammate Experience teams to optimize agent workflows, internal tooling, and back-office processes. Translate insights into actionable recommendations that inform strategy, prioritize investments, and improve member outcomes. Build measurement frameworks, dashboards, and reporting to drive performance monitoring and data-driven decisions. Leverage AI tools to accelerate analyses, enhance problem-solving, and continuously explore emerging capabilities and applications. Evaluate IVR and conversational AI experiences, developing measurement frameworks to assess effectiveness and member outcomes. What you’ll need: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Engineering, or another quantitative field; Master's degree preferred. 4+ years of relevant experience in Data Science or Analytics. Strong SQL and Python/R skills, with proficiency in data visualization tools such as Tableau. Demonstrated experience designing and evaluating A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and other causal inference methodologies. Strong foundation in statistics, analytical problem-solving, KPI development, and root cause analysis. Experience with operational, customer experience, or contact center analytics, including funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation, and performance measurement. Ability to connect operational metrics to customer or member outcomes and translate findings into actionable business recommendations. Strong business acumen, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to independently drive ambiguous analytical projects from problem definition through execution and impact measurement. Nice to have: Experience in fintech, financial services, or other regulated industries. Experience partnering with Operations, Contact Center, Customer Support, or Member Experience teams. Familiarity with operational metrics such as first contact resolution, contact rates, average handle time, escalation rates, manual review rates, and processing turnaround times. Exposure to conversational AI, IVR systems, chatbot analytics, or AI evaluation methodologies. Experience with dbt, Airflow, and Snowflake. jobs.title: Talent AI Operator
jobs.jd:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Help make autonomous recruiting work by supervising AI-powered candidate pipelines and stepping in when human judgment is needed. You will work across recruiting operations, product, and engineering to improve agent quality and define effective ways for people and AI to work together.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Monitor candidate conversations and intervene when an AI agent makes an error or needs human judgment.

 - Handle high-stakes conversations with senior candidates, including objections and compensation negotiations.

 - Review and label AI outputs, providing feedback and examples that improve agent performance.

 - Audit candidate matches, outreach quality, and conversion metrics across recruiting pipelines.

 - Guide candidates through final hiring stages, manage offers, and help close placements.

 - Document effective practices, create standard operating procedures, and build operational playbooks.

 - Collaborate with product, engineering, and leadership teams to improve recruiting operations.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - At least 2 years of experience in talent operations, recruiting, or sourcing at early-stage technology startups.

 - Hands-on experience using AI tools to evaluate output quality, identify errors, and assess AI capabilities and limitations.

 - Experience closing placements and managing final-stage candidate conversations, including offer negotiation and objection handling.

 - Experience using recruiting data, such as KPIs, dashboards, A/B tests, or conversion analysis, to inform decisions.

 - Experience training, labeling, or providing feedback to improve AI or machine learning systems or agent performance.

 - Ability to work cross-functionally in a startup environment; familiarity with TypeScript or JavaScript, Python, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, or Supabase is useful.

 - Experience with AI-focused startups or AI-native hiring processes, and a record of documenting processes or building operational playbooks.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Competitive base compensation plus uncapped performance-based pay tied to placements. Performance-based equity grants may be available following a successful 90-day performance period. Health insurance and visa sponsorship are available.


LOCATION

Hybrid in San Francisco, California.

jobs.title: Quantitative Analyst
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE


ABOUT THE ROLE

Quant Analysts build and improve the models that drive Base’s Trading & Risk platform - the system that spans our distributed fleet of batteries and the households we serve. You’ll own the price models that tell Base where value exists in wholesale markets like ERCOT and PJM, and the hedging strategy that turns that analysis into a plan for managing Base’s risk.

This is a mid-to-senior role that combines quantitative analysis, software engineering, and energy market expertise. Base has a price model for ERCOT that provides the foundation for future improvements. You’ll extend that work to PJM, sharpen how Base captures grid congestion, and use what you build to shape Base’s hedging strategy there.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Improve Base’s price distributions by capturing grid congestion effects, like midday price excursions regularly seen, that our current models miss

 - Build a price model for PJM, so Base can track risk and make hedging decisions there as well as it already does in ERCOT

 - Build a hedging strategy for PJM, using the models you build to decide what that strategy should be




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets and domain knowledge: you understand wholesale energy market operations like ERCOT, including real-time arbitrage, ancillary services, and capacity, along with unit commitment, economic dispatch, and production cost modeling

 - Coding and SQL: you build models in Python (or another language) and pull your own data with SQL, and you can work through a model independently

 - Statistics and machine learning: You understand the bias-variance tradeoff, train/validation/test evaluation, and loss functions for categorical and continuous targets, and you’re deeply familiar with at least one statistical subfield, like extreme value theory, information theory, or stochastic processes. You’ve deployed models to production with versioning and maintenance, scaled training beyond a single machine, and know Python, pandas, and visualization libraries well.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight — a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

jobs.title: Data Scientist 1
jobs.jd: Data Scientist 1 As our Data Scientist, you will act as an internal business consultant to help optimize every facet of this organization. You will solve problems and answer questions – using data – for other departments to help us reduce costs, reduce errors, and be a better organization for our 17 million members. Note: This is a hybrid role; the candidate must reside within a 100-mile radius of our Coppell TX office and be available to work on-site 3 days a week on a regular basis, as well as 2–3 times per month for team meetings and collaboration days. What You’ll Do Every day, you will help solve business problems presented to us by stakeholders using data. You will get a scenario or problem, such as, “We need to reduce cycle times,” and then pull, analyze, and interpret data relevant to that scenario. You will pull data from SQL databases. You will analyze and interpret data using Python, R, or other tools. You will determine patterns or trends and their statistical significance to the problem. To visualize the data, you will use Tableau. Once you have done your analysis, paired with a data engineer, you will present your findings to the stakeholder and confirm, refute or simply acknowledge a hypothesis. Your work may be implemented or may develop into something else. What You’ll Need To thrive in this role, you must have a solid foundation of statistics and data analysis. You must be able to describe a project where you pulled data, analyzed it, identified trends or patterns, determined significance, and delivered insights or recommendations to the business. What was your approach? What tools did you use and why? Did you get to the root cause of the issue? Did you confirm or refute a hypothesis? You must be able to speak to your involvement and decisions at each stage. For pulling data, we use SQL so you must be proficient with this tool. To curate and analyze data, we use a variety of languages and programs: Python, R, and even Excel. You can choose whatever tool helps you best, but you must be proficient in either Python or R. Excellent communication skills and an attitude of flexibility are a must. Very often, we get into the data and some aspect takes longer than we thought, or we have to pivot and change how we approach a problem. A dashboard works better than a model, perhaps. Then you have to explain to the stakeholder or the team why you made that change or why the deliverable is taking longer than expected. It’s all about being creative in your approach and communicating that frequently and clearly to people who may be less tech or data-savvy than you. You have worked previously with an Agile team or understand these concepts. You expect to participate in daily standup meetings, you’ll complete your projects or stories during our bimonthly sprints, and you’re ready to meet frequent deployment deadlines. #LI - SH1 Remarkable benefits: • Health coverage for medical, dental, vision • 401(K) saving plans with company match AND Pension • Tuition assistance • Floating holidays and PTO for community volunteer programs • Paid parental leave • Wellness programs • Employee discounts (membership, insurance, travel, entertainment, services and more!) The strength of our organization is our employees. Bringing together and supporting different cultures, backgrounds, personalities, and strengths creates a team capable of delivering legendary, lifetime service to our members. When we embrace our diversity – we win. All of Us! With our national brand recognition, long-standing reputation since 1900, and constantly growing membership, we are seeking career-minded, service-driven professionals to join our team. The healthcare industry overspends on its supply chain by over $25B each year, the result of fragmented data, inefficient workflows, and wasted supplies. Clarium is fixing that. Our AI-powered platform, Astra OS, gives hospitals end-to-end visibility into their supply chain operations, automating workflows and surfacing actionable insights so supply chain teams can focus on what matters most: patient care. You will work within the Clarium platform developing dashboards, AI automations, and innovative new solutions to drive efficiency and ensure continuity of patient care.

You will take ownership of maintaining the solutions that live in product, and you will be the team's resource on supply chain operations, especially inventory. We are looking for someone who is comfortable with data and technology and who knows healthcare supply chain operations well enough to spot what a dashboard or automation needs to get right. As a Finance Manager, you'll take ownership of financial models and analytics that shape our go-to-market strategy for the North America Consumer business. Your financial expertise will guide critical pricing decisions and strategic tradeoffs, establishing foundational capabilities with significant business impact. In this role, you'll partner with business leaders to optimize investment strategies, build robust financial models, and communicate insights to executive leadership. jobs.jd: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description Quantitative Analyst, Municipal Fixed Income Your Team The Quantitative Analyst will be part of the broader quantitative team supporting Invesco Fixed Income. The team develops market research, data, models, and analytical tools that strengthen investment decision-making, portfolio construction, and risk management. This role will focus on municipal strategies and work closely with portfolio managers and credit researchers on market, portfolio, and security-level questions. The analyst will also partner with quantitative, technology, and data colleagues to build reliable data and reusable analytical capabilities. Your Role As a Quantitative Analyst, you will combine municipal market knowledge, quantitative analysis, and practical implementation to support portfolio managers and credit researchers. You will identify and evaluate investment questions involving relative value, portfolio positioning, risk, performance, and market structure and build the tools needed to test and apply your ideas. You will have end-to-end responsibility for the municipal data supporting this work, from understanding source systems and resolving discrepancies to producing controlled analytical datasets. The role requires curiosity about markets and an interest in the daily work of turning data and investment ideas into reliable, useful analytics. You Will Be Responsible For: Generating and evaluating quantitative investment ideas related to municipal relative value, portfolio positioning, performance drivers, and market opportunities. Measuring portfolio exposures on an absolute and benchmark-relative basis, including interest-rate, yield-curve, spread, credit, liquidity, and optionality risks. Developing scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess how market changes could affect performance, volatility, distributions, and portfolio positioning. Investigating differences between expected and realized performance, distinguishing market and economic drivers from data or model issues, and communicating findings to portfolio managers and credit researchers. Evaluating leverage and funding risks, including tender option bond and variable-rate municipal term preferred exposures and their implications for total return, liquidity, and distributions. Managing municipal data end to end, including acquisition, definitions, transformations, timing, lineage, quality controls, reconciliation, and availability across systems such as Perform and Aladdin. Building and maintaining analytical tools and automated workflows for holdings, transactions, pricing, benchmarks, risk, and performance while reducing routine manual processing. Partnering with investment, quantitative, technology, and data colleagues to test new ideas, implement useful analytics, and contribute reusable data, methods, and code to the broader platform. The Experience You Bring: Experience applying quantitative analysis to fixed-income markets, relative value, portfolio risk, performance attribution, or portfolio construction. Knowledge of municipal securities, market conventions, portfolio structures, benchmarks, and sources of risk, or relevant fixed-income experience and a demonstrated ability to develop new market expertise. Demonstrated ability to formulate investment or analytical questions and build practical tools, models, or applications to evaluate them. Strong hands-on Python and SQL skills, including experience working with complex datasets and automating analytical workflows. Experience investigating data from multiple systems, reconciling inconsistencies, establishing data-quality controls, and developing reliable analytical datasets. Familiarity with modern development practices and platforms such as Git or GitHub, cloud infrastructure, Snowflake, Databricks, or comparable technologies. Experience using AI-assisted research or development tools to explore ideas, develop code, test analytical approaches, or improve productivity. Strong judgment and communication skills, including the ability to connect technical analysis to market developments, portfolio exposures, and practical investment decisions. The salary range for this position in New York City is 145,000 - 158,000 USD/year. The total compensation offered for this position includes salary and incentive pay and will vary based on skills, experience and location Full Time / Part Time Full time Worker Type Employee Job Exempt (Yes / No) Yes Workplace Model Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The job holder may be required to perform other duties as deemed appropriate by their manager from time to time. Invesco's culture of inclusivity and its commitment to diversity in the workplace are demonstrated through our people practices. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, citizenship status, disability, age, or veteran status. Our equal opportunity employment efforts comply with all applicable U.S. state and federal laws governing non-discrimination in employment.

jobs.title: Data Science Analyst
jobs.jd: Data Science Analyst Locations: Wilmington, DE (Hybrid) As an Associate Data Science Analyst, you’ll develop the technical skills to build the machine learning systems that drive our company and produce great customer outcomes. You’ll get hands-on experience as you apply your talents, creativity, and passion to create innovative solutions to real-world data science use cases. No matter the projects, you’ll have the opportunity to explore, while learning from experts in consumer lending in a close-knit team-oriented environment. This role will provide exposure across multiple disciplines to accelerate your career growth. In the Role: Apply diverse statistical and machine learning techniques to analyze a variety of datasets to solve complex, unstructured business problems. Actively contribute to our team’s vibrant culture through sharing knowledge, helping peers, and generally being a great person to work with. Develop creative technical solutions to improve the company’s decision making, the customer’s experience, and shareholder returns. Evaluate non-traditional data sources to see if they result in better underwriting decisions, saving our hard-working customers millions in interest payments. Mine the “digital exhaust” of our marketing campaigns to identify new populations who would benefit from our products. Partner with our operations teams to surface data insights that will allow our thousands of branch staff to better serve our customers. Requirements: Current post-graduate degree student in a quantitative discipline (Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Biostatistics, Physics, Economics, Operations Research, or Computer Science) graduating between December 2026 and June 2027. Outstanding communication skills, including the ability to explain technical topics and concepts to a non-technical audience. Proven experience (in an academic, athletic, volunteer, or employment context) working with teams of diverse individuals to deliver complex projects. Experience in use of open-source machine learning libraries (Python or R). Innovative and capable of developing creative solutions to complex, data-driven problems. Preferred: Successful candidates will possess strong analytic, strategic thinking, communications, and leadership skills. They will also demonstrate curiosity, creative problem solving, integrative business thinking, teamwork, and bias for action. Just as importantly, they will be enthusiastic learners who want to tackle real-world challenges. About You: You are ready to launch your data science career. You want to create solutions to help hard-working Americans improve their financial lives. You want to work on a modern cloud-based data infrastructure. You want to directly learn from some of the best data science and business leaders in consumer finance. You want to be part of a team which is nimble, collaborative, diverse, and fun. Who we Are: OneMain Financial (NYSE: OMF) is the leader in offering nonprime customers responsible access to credit and is dedicated to improving the financial well-being of hardworking Americans. Since 1912, we’ve looked beyond credit scores to help people get the money they need today and reach their goals for tomorrow. Our growing suite of personal loans, credit cards and other products help people borrow better and work toward a brighter future. Driven collaborators and innovators, our team thrives on transformative digital thinking, customer-first energy and flexible work arrangements that grow lives, careers and our company. At every level, we’re committed to an inclusive culture, career development and impacting the communities where we live and work. Getting people to a better place has made us a better company for over a century. There’s never been a better time to shine with OneMain. Because team members at their best means OneMain at our best, we provide opportunities and benefits that make their health and careers a priority. That’s why we’ve packed our comprehensive benefits package for full- and some part-time employees with: Health and wellbeing options including medical, prescription, dental, vision, hearing, accident, hospital indemnity, and life insurances Up to 4% matching 401(k) Employee Stock Purchase Plan (10% share discount) Tuition reimbursement Paid time off (15 days vacation per year) Paid sick leave as determined by state or local ordinance, prorated based on start date Paid holidays (11 days per year, based on start date) Paid volunteer time (3 days per year, prorated based on start date) Most Loved Workplace 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 OneMain Holdings, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer. THE JOB We are looking for a self-motivated, hardworking, team player to manage a portfolio of live event tickets. This role is critical to the success of our clients as you will help create and execute/implement the pricing strategy of our client’s ticket inventory. In this role, you will utilize our products, tools and reporting to analyze many different variables to determine the proper price and sales velocity for our client’s inventory. In addition, you will be directly communicating your findings to clients and management. WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING Create a pricing plan that is structured to achieve client goals. Analyze sales and demand data to identify trends and recommend pricing strategies. Own and track KPIs, including revenue, sell-through, margin percentage, and conversion rate, to evaluate personal and client event performance. Maintain a pricing schedule ensure all work is completed on time and at the proper cadence. Communicate and work with clients, internal teams and external marketplaces to resolve operational issues. Monitor real-time sales and market data to adjust pricing strategies and ensure client goals. Build and develop relationship with key external stakeholders. Create and present data driven power point decks to update clients on a weekly basis. Create visualizations and maintain dashboards using Domo/Data Visualization Tools. External and Internal Ad Hoc Requests. WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (or TECHNICAL SKILLS) Bachelor’s Degree in economics, Business Administration, Finance, or quantitative related field. Minimum 2+ years in an analytical role. Experience in ticketing, sports, or entertainment industry is a plus! Demonstrated experience in creating sales models and forecasts. jobs.title: Research Data Analyst
jobs.jd: The Research Data Analyst will work under the direction of Co-Directors of the Center for Biosignal Research (CBR) and report directly to the CBR Scientific Program Manager. The CBR at UCSF focuses on the study and clinical use of biosignals, or signals that can be continuously measured and monitored from the human body. Our areas of research broadly focus on improving biosignal analysis through signal processing and advanced algorithms, identifying predictors of adverse outcomes, using biosignals to improve physiologic understanding and leveraging these insights to improve patient care and reduce false alarms in bedside monitoring. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience with complex data analysis, in particular time-series data analysis, biomedical/clinical informatics, and/or signal processing, to develop and evaluate algorithms to interpret continuous bedside monitoring data, integrating additional clinical data such as electronic medical records when appropriate. Prior experience with clinical or biosignal data is preferred but not required. Example projects include the development of algorithms to improve alerting systems for clinically significant arrhythmias and other events, using monitoring data to predict patient trajectories within specific disease cohorts, or assessing the impact of changing alerting mechanisms on overall alarm burden in retrospective data. There are also opportunities to contribute to the design and implementation of the data and computing infrastructure that underlie these efforts. The incumbent will work independently and in collaboration with CBR staff and faculty investigators to facilitate multiple research projects and CBR efforts. jobs.title: Finance Analyst
jobs.jd:
Flex is building AI-native financial services for business owners.

 

We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.

 

Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.

 

Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.

 

Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.

 

- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.

- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.

- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.

- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

 

Team & Locations

 

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

 

Flex Fuels Ambition.

Team & Locations

 

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

 

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About Us

 - This is a ground-floor seat on a small finance team, and it's a genuinely embedded one. Most of your week will be spent with our go-to-market org — reporting on what our growth spend is actually returning, and acting as the finance counterpart on deal structure and pricing. The rest goes to the budget cycle, where you'll sit with department leads to build and defend their plans.
   
   We're hiring for judgment and speed, not years served. If you're two years out of a banking analyst program, or a strong new grad who models well and writes clearly, you're the profile. You'll report to our Director of FP&A and get real exposure to the exec team.

What You'll Do

 - Be the finance partner to go-to-market
   
   - Own reporting on the ROI of our growth investments — by channel, campaign, and segment — so the team knows what's working and what to cut
   
   - Run Deal Desk: serve as the finance liaison on pricing, deal structure, and non-standard terms, and be the person go-to-market pulls in before a deal gets committed
   
   - Build and maintain the customer and growth economics that inform how we invest in acquisition
   
   - Sit in go-to-market's meetings, not just their inbox — translate their questions into analysis and hand back a recommendation instead of a spreadsheet
   
   Run the budget cycle with the teams
   
   - Partner with department leads through quarterly budget and headcount planning — collect inputs, pressure-test them, and translate them into the plan
   
   - Track spend against budget, surface drift before it compounds, and flag what needs a decision
   
   - Build the analysis behind headcount, vendor, and resourcing calls — payback, cost-to-serve, build-vs-buy
   
   Support forecasting and reporting
   
   - Support the monthly forecast cycle: pull and reconcile actuals, build the variance analysis, and draft the commentary that explains what moved and why
   
   - Maintain the schedules and drivers that feed the company operating model, working alongside the Director of FP&A
   
   - Help assemble the monthly and quarterly reporting packages for leadership, the board, and lenders
   
   Automate anything you do twice
   
   - Replace recurring manual work with something durable — AI workflows, queries, dashboards, templates — so next month it takes minutes
   
   - Bring rigor to automated output: reconcile it, stress it, and know where it breaks before someone else finds out

Requirements

 - 

 - 0–2 years in FP&A, strategic finance, investment banking, consulting, Big 4, or a comparably analytical role — exceptional new grads welcome

 - Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field

 - You build financial models from a blank sheet. Advanced Excel or Google Sheets is table stakes here, not a bullet point

 - Hands-on exposure to a real budgeting or forecasting cycle

 - AI is already the default in how you work, and you have the judgment to go with it: a reliable instinct for when a machine-generated answer is wrong, and the discipline to check before you forward it

 - You write clearly. You can compress a 40-tab model into three sentences a founder can act on

 - Extreme attention to detail, and comfort operating in ambiguity at speed — priorities here change faster than the plan does

 - Based in the US


NICE TO HAVES

 - SQL — you can pull your own data instead of filing a ticket

 - Python, or comparable scripting for analysis and automation

 - BI and analytics tooling (Looker, Tableau, Power BI, Hex) and modern planning tools (Pigment, Cube, Aleph, NetSuite)

 - Fintech, banking, or lending background

Why Join Us

 

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.

Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.

Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.

True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.

Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.

High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.

Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.

Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

They use technical know-how, excellent problem-solving skills, user insights, and proactive communication to protect users and our partners from abuse across Google products like Search, Maps, Gmail, and Google Ads. On this team, you're a big-picture thinker and strategic team-player with a passion for doing what’s right. You work globally and cross-functionally with Google engineers and product managers to identify and fight abuse and fraud cases at Google speed - with urgency. And you take pride in knowing that every day you are working hard to promote trust in Google and ensuring the highest levels of user safety. We are on a critical mission to protect Google’s users and ensure online safety across core and emerging Ads products. The Content Safety team is at the frontline of this commitment, blending technical data analysis with policy enforcement and abuse mitigation to protect our users, partners, and advertisers. As a Trust and Safety Analyst in Ads Content Safety, you are responsible for safeguarding the Ads ecosystem by detecting, investigating, and mitigating policy violations and abuse vectors at scale. You do not just react to threats; you use large-scale data and technical tooling to identify systemic vulnerabilities, influence how engineering and product teams design detection systems, and deploy scalable solutions without compromising legitimate advertiser experiences. At Google we work hard to earn our users’ trust every day. Trust & Safety is Google’s team of abuse fighting and user trust experts working daily to make the internet a safer place. We partner with teams across Google to deliver bold solutions in abuse areas such as malware, spam and account hijacking. A team of Analysts, Policy Specialists, Engineers, and Program Managers, we work to reduce risk and fight abuse across all of Google’s products, protecting our users, advertisers, and publishers across the globe in over 40 languages. Execute complex queries and investigations to analyze abuse trends, uncover scam patterns, identify product vulnerabilities, and influence system improvements. Identify automation and efficiency opportunities, driving impactful solutions through deep analysis and robust cross-functional partnerships. jobs.title: Sales Operations Database Administrator
jobs.jd: Objective: Sales Operations at Fortinet manages systems and databases used by all the employees in Sales plus other departments. Over the past 10 years the data architecture and decisions from Sales Ops meant that our BI tools became first class, we are looking for someone to help us with the continuous search for better technologies. A core part of this role is helping build out our AI capabilities – the data infrastructure you administer will increasingly serve as the foundation of LLM powered tools. Responsibilities: Maintain API Jobs: our data comes from different places at Fortinet, most of these processes are written in Python, the successful applicant will be expected to maintain, improve and add new processes. Database work: we currently run most of our data under Microsoft SQL, we also leverage Mongo and Postgres. You will be expected to maintain ETL scripts and other SQL Queries that make our BI Tool (Tableau) operate. We also expect you to manage indexing, cleanups and good performance practices. Exploring new solutions: you will be expected to proactively review and help assess new tools that can make our processes better and faster, as technology changes and LLMs become more frequently used, we need to make sure our databases can handle future workload. Enable AI capabilities: you will play a key role in building and maintaining the data foundation that powers AI and LLM-based tools across the organization. CRM Work: even though we don’t work inside the CRM, you will be expected to understand how a CRM works and how sales uses a CRM, this will be helpful when importing datasets and understanding how to build efficient queries for sales. Investigative approach: the applicant must have the instinct of being curious, our team is continuously learning new technologies and building new applications for sales, we expect you to keep up and bring new ideas. Required Skills: Strong Python for building and maintaining data pipelines, API integrations, and automation scripts. Advanced SQL, with hands-on experience in RDBMS and data lakes. Experience monitoring database systems for capacity and performance. Proven experience designing and maintaining ETL processes feeding BI/reporting tools. Database performance tuning: indexing strategy, query optimization, data cleanup, and general good-hygiene practices. Experience with Tableau as a data source owner, not just a report consumer. Working understanding of how CRMs operate and how sales teams use them (Salesforce experience a plus), enough to model and import sales datasets sensibly. Comfort integrating and consuming REST APIs from varied internal and third-party sources. Location: Candidate should be in the Sunnyvale, CA area. Fortinet offers employees a variety of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, 401(k), 11 paid holidays, vacation time, and sick time as well as a comprehensive leave program. Wage ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, and job level. On target earnings for this position is expected to be $140,000 - $160,000 per year. Exact salary offers will be determined by factors such as the candidate's subject knowledge, skill level, qualifications, experience, and geographic location. All roles are eligible to participate in the Fortinet equity program, and this position is also eligible for commissions based on the terms of the Sales Compensation Plan

jobs.title: Client Consulting Analyst
jobs.jd: About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world. Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you. Job Description Overview: Visa Consulting and Analytics (VCA) is the consulting arm of Visa and drives tangible, impactful results for clients. Drawing on our expertise in consulting, data analytics, technology, payments and economics, VCA solves the most strategic problems for our clients. The core client segments of VCA include issuers, acquirers, merchants, fintechs, payment enablers and governments. Role Summary: The Analyst for Digital, Strategy and AI supports the delivery of digital transformation, strategy and artificial intelligence (AI) engagements across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. The Digital, Strategy and AI Consulting practice is a team of experts specializing in strategy and digital transformation topics, including but not limited to: Strategy: Defining business, segment, channel and functional strategies, such as digital banking, affluent banking, loyalty, open finance, stablecoins and artificial intelligence. Ideation: Supporting the innovation agenda of clients through foresight, strategic trends research and co-creation activities. Value proposition design: Developing holistic offerings, including products, services and customer experience, for strategic consumer, business and corporate customer segments. Customer experience and engagement: Developing best-in-class digital customer journeys and engagement strategies, including digital onboarding, end-to-end digital journey transformation, digital channel benchmarking and user interface and user experience enhancement. Performance analytics: Improving client performance and process efficiency by deploying data, digital and AI tools. Digital delivery: Supporting clients with the implementation of digital strategies, including the design and development of digital channels, generative AI (GenAI) use cases and proofs of concept. Key Responsibilities: As an Analyst, you will work within project teams under the guidance of senior consultants and managers, contributing to research, analysis and the development of client deliverables. Support the delivery of digital, strategy and AI projects across the GCC, from scoping through to final recommendations. Conduct market, competitor and customer research, including benchmarking and trends analysis, to inform client recommendations. Gather, clean and analyze data from Visa and industry sources to generate insights that support client recommendations. Contribute to the problem-solving process, including structuring analytical frameworks and developing insight-driven recommendations. Build business cases and financial models that measure business performance and quantify return on investment (ROI). Prepare clear and compelling client presentations and reports that communicate findings and recommendations. Support the preparation and running of client workshops and stakeholder sessions, and document findings, decisions and next steps. Track project workplans and deliverables, and keep the project leadership informed of progress, risks and issues. Collaborate with Visa Account Executives and the Product, Value-Added Services (VAS), Marketing and other internal teams to deliver integrated solutions as One Visa. Contribute to proposals and responses to requests for proposal (RFPs), as well as practice thought leadership, points of view and case studies. Help build reusable toolkits, templates and best practice documents that can be applied across the VCA practice. Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. Qualifications Basic Qualifications: At least 2 years of work experience in management consulting, preferably on financial services, payments, digital or AI projects. Degree from a leading university, preferably in business, economics, engineering, computer science or a related field. Professional proficiency in English. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel, including building clear and compelling presentations, financial models and data analyses. Strong curiosity about AI, including GenAI and agentic AI, with hands-on experience using AI tools for research, analysis or content creation and an understanding of how to use them responsibly. Preferred Qualifications: Experience working on projects in the GCC region. Exposure to digital transformation, strategy or digital banking projects. Knowledge of banking products, services, operations; payment schemes, services, card issuing and marketing initiatives. Strong interest in fintech and payments. Proficiency in Arabic is a plus. What You Will Need to Be Successful: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex problems and work with large data sets. Strong storytelling skills, with the ability to turn analysis into clear and compelling presentations. Excellent oral and written communication skills. Commercial awareness and an understanding of the financial indicators used to measure business performance. A collaborative, diplomatic and flexible working style, with the ability to work effectively in a matrixed organization. High attention to detail and a commitment to deliverables quality. Self-motivated and results-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines at the same time. Curiosity and a willingness to learn, take on feedback and develop new skills quickly. Ability to build strong working relationships with clients and colleagues. Visa is an EEO Employer Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

Manage, transform, and integrate portfolio and benchmark data to support advanced quantitative analysis, ensuring information is accurate, auditable, and analytically robust. Design and deliver custom analyses and models to answer ad‑hoc investment, portfolio management, and investor questions. Identify, define, and refine key investment metrics and analytical views that inform investment decisions and support positive business outcomes. Build and maintain Power BI dashboards that combine quantitative outputs and visual storytelling to support portfolio management and senior leadership. Partner with investment, finance, and investor relations teams to support due diligence, investor requests, marketing materials, and quarterly performance reporting. Engage users with analytically rigorous tools and datasets, creating a virtuous cycle where insights drive adoption and improved data quality. Configure eFront and assist users with troubleshooting and best practices. Contribute to the design and maintenance of AI‑ready datasets by optimizing and enhancing datasets for consumption by investment professionals. Clearly document analytical methodologies, assumptions, data standards, and repeatable processes. What You'll Bring to the Role: Bachelor’s and/or master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Financial Engineering, or a related quantitative field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Two or more years of experience in a quantitative, analytics, investment, or performance measurement‑focused role. Experience with investment performance measurement, return calculations, or portfolio analytics. jobs.title: Data Scientist, Integrity
jobs.jd:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.

jobs.title: AI GTM Specialist, Model Hub
jobs.jd:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.






ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling Model Hub gives scientists access to AI models for biologics and small molecule discovery, including Lilly TuneLab models. Our goal is to give every scientist easy access to running models at scale and help model developers distribute their latest advancements. You’ll be the first hire dedicated to Model Hub adoption. You’ll find computational biology and other dry lab teams, introduce them to Model Hub, and work hands-on with them to get models running in their workflows. You’ll also own TuneLab onboarding for Benchling customers.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Reach out and engage computational biology, data science, and other dry lab leaders at customers

 - Work directly with customers to understand their science and recommend how models in Benchling (e.g. structure/property prediction, generative models) can be applied

 - Deliver Model Hub demos and lead technical workshops, including on integrating our API and MCP for running models

 - Onboard TuneLab members, from access setup through first model runs and setting up data contributions for federated learning

 - Collect customer feedback and work with the Model Hub team to prioritize and implement it

 - Build collateral (decks, notebooks, example workflows, talk tracks) as we learn which use cases land

 - Coordinate with partners, including Lilly TuneLab and model developers, on onboarding and new model rollouts

 


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2-4 years in a technical customer-facing role (solutions engineering, field application science, technical sales) or on a computational biology or other dry lab team

 - Working knowledge of protein or small molecule modeling (e.g. AlphaFold, ESMFold, antibody developability or ADMET models)

 - Comfort with Python and APIs. You can debug a customer’s model run yourself.

 - Comfort presenting to scientific leaders and running a technical workshop

 - Bias toward action in ambiguity. This product and this role are both being built in real time.

What success looks like in the first 6 months

 - Increase in Model Hub adoption across biotech and pharma companies

 - Engaging dry lab leaders, running demos, and onboarding TuneLab customers independently

 - A repeatable Model Hub onboarding playbook (workshop format, pilot structure, example workflows) in use across customers

 - A set of customer case studies that show measurable value from Model Hub

 


HOW WE WORK

This is an in-person team in San Francisco built around collaborating in the office in a fast-paced environment. We’re in the office Monday through Friday. 




Benchling welcomes everyone.

We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences.

Job Description This role focuses on Internal Liquidity Stress Testing (ILST), liquidity risk strategy, quantitative analysis, and emerging risk identification. The Analyst will assess how changes in the balance sheet, funding markets, customer behavior, and broader financial conditions affect the firm’s liquidity position under normal and stressed environments. The role combines financial analysis, data analytics, and risk management, with exposure to senior Treasury and Risk stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Support the execution, analysis, and ongoing enhancement of the firm’s Internal Liquidity Stress Testing (ILST) framework, including assumptions, scenarios, documentation, controls, and data validation. Perform scenario, sensitivity, trend, and period-over-period analysis to identify key drivers and emerging liquidity risks. Monitor balance-sheet and financial-market developments, including deposit behavior, wholesale and secured funding, collateral, and market liquidity. Forecast liquidity needs on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis to help inform funding decisions. Work with large financial and regulatory datasets to identify trends, anomalies, concentrations, and unexpected movements. Use tools such as Excel, SQL, Python, and Power BI to support analysis, reporting, and process improvements. Investigate complex or unexpected results, challenge assumptions using data, and translate findings into clear conclusions for technical and non-technical audiences. Identify opportunities to automate recurring analytics and improve the efficiency and repeatability of existing processes. Strong Excel skills and comfort working with large datasets. Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy. Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly in written and verbal formats. Intellectual curiosity, willingness to learn, strong work ethic, and ability to work effectively as part of a team. Internship, coursework, or experience in banking, Treasury, balance-sheet management/ALM, financial markets, risk management, financial analysis, or data analytics. Exposure to SQL, Python, Power BI, VBA, coding, or other analytical tools. Familiarity with bank balance sheets, deposits, securities, wholesale funding, capital markets, or liquidity risk concepts such as ILST, LCR, HQLA, and liquidity stress testing. Familiarity with regulatory or financial datasets such as FR Y-9C, FR Y-15, FR 2052a, Call Reports, or Federal Reserve H.8 is helpful but not required. JOB DESCRIPTION: Finance Rotational Analyst Charlotte, NC – hybrid The Driven Brands Finance Rotation Program is a 24-month early-career program designed to provide broad exposure across our Finance organization through four six-month rotations. The Finance Rotational Analyst will contribute to real business priorities while building experience in financial and data analysis, problem-solving, communication, and relationship management. Working with different teams and leaders throughout the program, the participants will understand how various areas of Finance operate and identify where their own interests and strengths may fit over the long term. The Development Experience The 24-month program includes structured training, regular manager coaching, a dedicated Program Sponsor, and long-term mentoring. Participants will gain exposure to different areas of the business while developing skills in communication, critical thinking, business acumen, and data analysis. At the end of the program, successful participants will be considered for full-time Finance opportunities based on performance, career interests, business needs, and available roles. What you’ll Drive: Complete four six-month rotations across Finance and related support functions. Perform financial, operational, and data analysis to help teams understand business performance and support informed decision-making. Take on the responsibilities of an entry-level team member within each rotation, contributing to the core day-to-day activities and priorities of the assigned function. Build an understanding of key business processes, financial drivers, performance measures, systems, and risks. Prepare presentations, analyses, and summaries that clearly communicate findings, actionable insights, and recommendations to key stakeholders. Collaborate with cross-functional teams and build relationships across the organization. Identify opportunities to improve processes, analyses, and ways of working. Apply critical-thinking and problem-solving skills to new or unfamiliar business questions. Take on additional responsibility and work more independently as you progress through each rotation. Participate in regular coaching, mentoring, and development discussions throughout the program. Complete the Finance Rotation Program's 24-month training curriculum. Establish annual development goals, seek and apply feedback, and reflect on your progress throughout the program. What you’ll Bring: Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Data Analytics, or another quantitative field. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills. Foundational proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Curiosity and an interest in understanding how different areas of a business operate. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with different teams and stakeholders. Willingness to ask questions, receive feedback, and apply what you learn. Strong organization and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple priorities and work both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment. Flexibility and willingness to learn new functions, systems, and responsibilities throughout the program. Added Fuel if you have: Previous internship experience in Finance, Accounting, Internal Audit, Business Analytics, Corporate Strategy, or a related field. Previous internship experience with Driven Brands. Experience using Microsoft Excel to analyze data. Exposure to financial statements, financial analysis, budgeting, or forecasting. Experience with business intelligence, data visualization, ERP, or other financial systems. Experience using AI or AI-enabled tools to support analysis, research, automation, data preparation, or process improvement. Demonstrated leadership through employment, academics, athletics, student organizations, volunteer work, or other extracurricular activities. jobs.jd: Portfolio Analyst - Associate Location: Boston, MA (Hybrid) Your Role As a Portfolio Analyst, you will play a high‑visibility role supporting the financial performance and strategic decision‑making of a diverse portfolio of data center assets. You will partner closely with Portfolio Management leadership, including Vice Presidents, Directors, and Asset Managers, to deliver financial analysis, forecasts, reporting, and recommendations that inform executive‑level decisions. Your work will have direct exposure to senior stakeholders and a visible impact on business outcomes. What you’ll do Develop, maintain, and analyze cash flow models for data center assets, including lease and investment analyses. Prepare investment analyses and underwriting materials for properties across multiple markets. Support deal, capital, and construction project presentations for the Investment Committee. Manage and consolidate annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, long‑term projections, and variance analyses. Validate monthly financial reports and support portfolio‑level reporting, including occupancy and capital planning. Track and analyze leasing activity, leasing statistics, and portfolio performance trends. Monitor construction and redevelopment activity, budgets, and development progress. Research market conditions, including supply, demand, competition, and broader market trends. Create and maintain financial reports, databases, and ad hoc analyses driven by market or lease activity. Support ad hoc reporting and general Asset Management administrative needs. What you’ll need Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Real Estate, or a related field. 0-2 years of experience in real estate analysis, such as asset management, development, lending, or commercial leasing. Strong understanding of real estate finance, including discounted cash flow modeling and financial reporting. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Working knowledge of Yardi preferred; familiarity with Argus is a plus. Ability to analyze large data sets, think strategically, and deliver detailed, well‑reasoned recommendations. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with strong attention to detail. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment. Collaborative, resourceful, and eager to learn, with the ability to adapt quickly to new tools and systems. Willingness to adopt AI‑enabled tools, accept feedback, go above and beyond expectations, and travel occasionally as needed. A bit about us Digital Realty brings companies and data together by delivering the full spectrum of data center, colocation and interconnection solutions. PlatformDIGITAL®, the company’s global data center platform, provides customers with a secure data meeting place and a proven Pervasive Datacenter Architecture (PDx®) solution methodology for powering innovation and efficiently managing Data Gravity challenges. Digital Realty gives its customers access to the connected data communities that matter to them with a global data center footprint of 300+ facilities in 50+ metros across 25+ countries on six continents. To learn more about Digital Realty, please visit digitalrealty.com or follow us on LinkedIn and Twitter . From managing budgets to financial and inventory planning, we deliver a full range of finance and strategic problem solving to help our business stay on track, support our customers, and meet our goals. What we can offer you Our rapidly evolving business sector offers the opportunity to be part of a courageous and passionate team who work together to understand and meet the changing needs of our global customers. Join us and you’ll be part of a supportive and inclusive environment where you can bring your whole self to work. As part of our team, you’ll get to work with people from different business areas, challenge the way we do things and put your ideas into action. We’ll also give you plenty of development opportunities so you can build a rewarding and successful career with us. Apply today, take charge of your career and grow your talents with us. Health and Safety Safety isn't just a priority here at Digital; it's critical to everything we do. Safeguarding lives, protecting assets, and securing data aren't just ideals - they're essential pillars of our commitment to excellence for our people, our partners and our customers. We have a culture of care where every member of Team Digital embraces a relentless pursuit of working safely across Digital Realty. Together we are Safely Powering Progress. Central to our compensation philosophy is rewarding our employees for achieving the values and objectives aligned to the company's overall goals and values.
