jobs.title: Strategy Analyst
jobs.jd: Job Summary The Strategy Analyst supports executive and health system leadership across the enterprise by translating complex internal, market, and industry datasets into actionable strategic insights. Operating within the Business Development department, this role focuses on evaluating market share dynamics, optimizing ambulatory and inpatient access points, supporting service line planning, and supporting enterprise capacity planning. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative modeling skills with healthcare domain fluency to inform capital allocation, network expansion, and long-term strategic planning. Essential Functions Market Share & Competitive Intelligence: Analyze external claims, state inpatient/outpatient discharge databases, and demographic data to evaluate market share trends, competitor positioning, migration patterns, and whitespace opportunities across primary and secondary service areas. Service Line Analytics: Partner with service line executives and physician leaders to assess clinical program performance, volume trajectories, payer mix shifts, contribution margins, and downstream referral patterns. Access Point & Network Optimization: Conduct geospatial and catchment area analyses to evaluate ambulatory footprint performance, site-of-care shifts, clinic utilization, and optimal locations for new facilities or service expansions. Capacity Planning & Demand Forecasting: Build quantitative models to project inpatient bed demand, procedural room utilization, and ambulatory capacity constraints based on population health trends, clinical acuity, and operational throughput. Executive Decision Support: Synthesize multi-source findings into clear, executive-ready presentations and business cases that guide strategic planning, partnership evaluations, and capital investments. ***Hybrid in Franklin, TN strongly preferred. Fully remote considered for standout candidates with exceptional experience*** Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Economics, Data Science, Finance, Statistics, Public Health, or a related quantitative field required; Master’s degree (MHA, MPH, MBA, or MS in Analytics) is strongly preferred. Experience: Minimum of 2–4 years of experience in healthcare strategy, management consulting, decision support, or quantitative analytics. Direct experience working within a hospital, multi-hospital health system, payer, or healthcare consulting environment strongly preferred. Technical Background: Experience working with large-scale healthcare datasets (e.g., Epic/Cerner EHR extracts, Cost Accounting/Decision Support systems, state/all-payer claims data, CMS datasets, or syndicated market intelligence platforms such as Sg2, Advisory Board, or Claritas). Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Healthcare Domain Knowledge: Understanding of hospital and ambulatory operations, healthcare reimbursement models, service line economics (e.g., DRGs, APCs, RVUs), and competitive market dynamics. Analytical & Data Visualization Skills: Proficiency in Excel for complex data analysis and financial/volume modeling; demonstrated ability to build intuitive visuals in Tableau, Power BI, or Excel. Strategic Communication: Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint to design clean, structured, executive-ready slide decks. Ability to distill technical analyses into concise business narratives for executives, clinical leaders, and other non-technical stakeholders. Project Management & Collaboration: Self-directed with strong organizational skills to manage multiple competing strategic initiatives simultaneously while maintaining rigorous attention to analytical accuracy.

jobs.title: 1000000934.STATISTICAL RESEARCH ANALYST.JAIL DIVERSION
jobs.jd: Performs advanced research and data analytics in support of the Criminal Justice Department and Dallas County criminal justice system, with primary responsibility for forecasting and projections, advanced statistical analysis, formal program evaluation, and data validation and quality assurance. Develops and applies analytical methodologies, statistical models, forecasts, and performance measures to identify trends, evaluate system and program outcomes, assess current and future operational needs, and ensure the accuracy, reliability, and appropriate interpretation of data used for decision-making. Translates complex data and research findings into actionable information and recommendations to support executive leadership, policymakers, criminal justice stakeholders, and other decisionmakers in operational, policy, budgetary, and strategic planning. Management Scope: Provides technical guidance and analytical support to departmental staff, interns, contractors, and project teams. May serve as lead analyst on research, evaluation, forecasting, and data-quality initiatives. May supervise exempt and non-exempt staff. Conducts advanced statistical and analytical studies of jail population, bookings, releases, length of stay, case processing, dispositions, demographic and behavioral health trends, recidivism, diversion, and other criminal justice system indicators; identifies trends, relationships, disparities, factors influencing system outcomes, operational barriers that prevent movement through the interagency dependent criminal justice system, including identifying process delays, system bottlenecks, handoffs and process failures across, and opportunities for operational and other system-level opportunities for improvement. Develops, maintains, validates, evaluates, and refines forecasting and projection models, including jail population forecasts, capacity projections, workload estimates, trend analyses, scenario modeling, and other predictive analyses used for operational, budgetary, and strategic planning. Designs and conducts formal program, policy, and process evaluations to assess effectiveness, efficiency, outcomes, and return on investment cost-benefit, cost-effectiveness, marginal-cost, and avoided-cost analysis; develops performance measures, benchmarks, methodologies, and evaluation frameworks; assesses whether programs and initiatives are achieving intended outcomes; and recommends program, policy, or process improvements based on findings. Extracts, integrates, validates, cleans, reconciles, and analyzes data from multiple criminal justice and administrative information systems; conducts data-quality and quality-assurance reviews; identifies anomalies, discrepancies, missing or inconsistent information, and reporting limitations; and assesses the accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability of data used for analysis and decision-making. Applies appropriate statistical and research methodologies, including descriptive and inferential statistics, regression analysis, time-series analysis, geospatial analysis, survival/event-history analysis, trend analysis, sampling, hypothesis testing, and other quantitative or qualitative methods appropriate to departmental research needs; documents methodologies, assumptions, limitations, and interpretations to support transparent and reproducible analysis. Develops dashboards, automated reports, data visualizations, executive summaries, research reports, presentations, and other analytical products; translates complex statistical findings into clear, understandable information and evidence-based, actionable recommendations for technical and nontechnical audiences. Provides research and analytical consultation to departmental leadership and criminal justice partners; supports strategic planning, policy development, grant applications and evaluations, budget and resource analyses, legislative or mandated reporting, ad hoc research requests, and cross-agency initiatives. Establishes and maintains documentation, data definitions, analytical standards, and quality-control procedures to promote consistent, accurate, and reproducible reporting. Performs other duties as assigned. Education, Experience and Training: Education and experience equivalent to a Master's degree from an accredited college or university in Statistics, Data Science, Analytics, Economics, Public Policy, Public Administration, Criminal Justice/Criminology, Sociology, Social Science Research, Applied Mathematics, Epidemiology, Operations Research, or a closely related quantitative or research-oriented field. Two (2) years of professional work-related experience. Special Requirements/Knowledge, Skills & Abilities: • Advanced knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, statistical analysis, research design, data analytics, forecasting, program evaluation, experimental and quasi-experimental methods, performance measurement, and data visualization. • Skill in analytical and data-visualization tools such as Microsoft Excel, SQL, Power BI, R, Python, SAS, SPSS, Stata or comparable applications, with demonstrated ability to learn and apply additional analytical technologies as required. • Knowledge of methods used to develop and validate statistical models, projections, forecasts, trend analyses, and performance measures. • Ability to evaluate model assumptions, limitations, accuracy, and reliability and clearly communicate uncertainty associated with projections and statistical findings. • Knowledge of data governance (development of cross-agency data definitions, data dictionaries, governance standards and standardized performance measures), data quality, validation, documentation, reproducibility, and quality-assurance practices. jobs.title: Growth Analytics
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is looking for an excellent operator to help scale the systems behind our customer acquisition engine.

This role is responsible for increasing the speed, intelligence, and effectiveness of how our customer acquisition team operates. You will drive experimentation, while building the systems, automation, and infrastructure that make that experimentation scalable.

The ideal candidate is highly resourceful, systems-oriented, technically curious, and obsessed with finding leverage. You should be equally comfortable thinking strategically, digging through data, building workflows, launching experiments, and executing quickly in ambiguous environments.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build systems, workflows, and dashboards that improve the speed and effectiveness of the customer acquisition team.

 - Drive experimentation across customer acquisition initiatives.

 - Build operational infrastructure that improves measurement, reporting, attribution, funnel visibility, and experimentation velocity.

 - Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Sales, and Member Experience teams to improve systems across the funnel.
   
    


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 1+ years of experience working in a fast-paced environment.

 - You are highly execution-oriented and naturally default toward building, shipping, and improving systems.

 - You’ve built workflows, operational systems, or experimentation frameworks that drove measurable business outcomes.

 - Strong systems thinking: you instinctively identify bottlenecks, friction, and opportunities for operational leverage.

 - Analytical ability and comfort working with data, funnels, attribution, experimentation, and customer behavior.

 - Ability to operate independently and execute quickly in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

 - Strong judgment and a bias toward action.

 - High ownership and accountability.
   
    


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Experience working large data sets in BigQuery (or similar data warehouses).

 - AI workflows, operational automation, or internal tooling that improved execution or business performance.

 - Strong analytics fluency, including SQL and product analytics platforms such as PostHog, Amplitude, or Mixpanel.

 - Experience with experimentation frameworks, funnel analysis, segmentation, and attribution systems.

 - Experience operating in high-growth startup environments.




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team at Base is lean, high-ownership, and results-driven. We operate with clear accountability, tight feedback loops, and a strong bias towards action. Marketing works closely with design, sales, and product to build scalable systems that support the rapid buildout of America's next-generation power company.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

This role combines policy analysis, data analytics, process improvement, and AI innovation to evaluate how governance requirements perform in practice, identify opportunities to improve effectiveness and usability, and help translate policy into scalable operational capabilities. The analyst will use data, stakeholder feedback, and implementation insights to inform policy decisions, support continuous improvement of governance frameworks, and develop AI-enabled solutions that make policy easier to understand, access, and operationalize. The ideal candidate is analytically minded, technologically curious, and passionate about using data and AI to make governance more effective, efficient, and scalable. Evaluate governance outcomes, implementation challenges, stakeholder feedback, and operational metrics to identify opportunities for improvement. Determine whether implementation challenges stem from policy design, process execution, technology limitations, or organizational factors. Recommend enhancements to policies, standards, guidance, and governance frameworks that improve effectiveness, scalability, and user experience while maintaining appropriate risk management objectives. Develop metrics, reporting, and insights that support data-driven policy decisions and demonstrate governance effectiveness. Support the development of implementation guidance, playbooks, and supporting materials that improve consistency and adoption. Translate policy requirements into machine-consumable knowledge, decision logic, workflows, and governance capabilities. Design, prototype, or support AI-enabled solutions that help users navigate governance requirements and make informed decisions. Build or support AI agents, copilots, knowledge solutions, and workflow automations that operationalize policy requirements. Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend practical applications that improve governance effectiveness and scalability. Gather, document, and prioritize requirements for policy enhancements, reporting capabilities, AI-enabled solutions, governance tooling, and process improvements. Translate analytical findings and stakeholder needs into actionable recommendations and implementation plans. jobs.title: People AI Operations Specialist
jobs.salary: $110K – $150K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • Multiple Ranges
jobs.jd:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.



The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.




OPERATING PRINCIPLES

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.




AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

 - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

 - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

 - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

 - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.



About the Role

We are building the next generation of People Operations at Deepgram. We're looking for a technically strong, AI-native builder to partner directly with our Director of People Operations to identify, design, build, and maintain AI-first workflows that fundamentally change how People and Talent operate, and then share what works with other teams across Deepgram.

This isn't a traditional systems or Operations admin role. You'll own the systems that sit on top of and between our People tools: connecting and configuring them through APIs, webhooks, and workflows, and turning manual, repetitive, high-friction People processes into intelligent workflows using AI, automation, internal tools, and agents. Just as importantly, you'll debug, maintain, and scale what you build so it keeps working as Deepgram grows.

You'll sit within People Operations and partner with Talent, IT, Security, Finance and other key functions to build secure, scalable solutions that allow team members and managers to get answers and complete workflows without requiring a People team member for every interaction.

This is a highly hands-on role for someone who loves building, experimenting, and turning operational chaos into order. You might be an early-career engineer, a career resetter, or a People Ops or talent operations professional who taught yourself to code and automate. What matters is what you can build, and that you want to build it for People.


What You'll Do

 - Partner directly with the People Operations and Talent teams to identify high-impact opportunities to apply AI and automation across systems.

 - Turn manual People workflows into automated, AI-powered systems.

 - Build AI agents and workflows that can answer questions, gather information, initiate processes, and complete defined actions.

 - Integrate AI systems with existing tools, including Ashby, Slack, Metaview, BambooHR, Lattice, Pave, Carta, and other internal systems.

 - Configure and connect our People tools beyond AI, including Ashby workflows, webhooks, APIs, and vendor integrations, so the team can move faster without relying on vendor support and walkthroughs.

 - Integrate AI systems with existing processes, including recruiting, onboarding, performance, and compensation.

 - Build an AI-first virtual onboarding experience that is scalable, and provides an exceptional team member experience.

 - Build internal tools and interfaces that make People processes dramatically easier for employees, managers, and the People team.

 - Prototype quickly, test with real users, learn from what works, and iterate.

 - Establish appropriate human-in-the-loop controls, escalation paths, permissions, and safeguards for sensitive People workflows.

 - Partner with Engineering and IT on architecture, security, access controls, and productionizing successful prototypes.

 - Measure whether what you build actually saves time, improves the employee experience, or increases the quality and consistency of People Operations.

jobs.jd: At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One. Job Description We are looking for someone who is curious, motivated to learn, and brings a positive, collaborative attitude to our Wholesale and Small Business Model Validation team. The role sits within the Model Risk Management department, part of the Risk Management and Compliance organization at U.S. Bank. As a Quantitative Model Validation Analyst, you will support the independent validation of CCAR and CECL credit loss forecasting models and risk rating scorecard models across commercial portfolios. These models are foundational to enterprise credit risk assessment, loss forecasting, reserving, and capital planning, offering a unique opportunity to deliver high-impact insights through rigorous analysis, clear documentation, and strong stakeholder engagement. Key Responsibilities: Conduct independent validation of the Bank’s wholesale and small business portfolio credit loss forecasting models supporting CCAR stress testing and CECL requirements. Evaluate model conceptual soundness, the reasonableness of assumptions, the reliability of data, the appropriateness of performance metrics, the effectiveness of model monitoring, and the adequacy of implementation testing. Design and execute validation testing, including benchmarking, sensitivity analysis, and outcome analysis, to assess model limitations, uncertainty, assumption risk, and forecast reasonableness. Identify emerging risks and assess the impact of evolving market conditions on model performance, conducting research to evaluate potential model degradation and associated model risk. Document and communicate validation outcomes and findings, ensuring model risks are accurately identified, timely escalated, and clearly understood by stakeholders and regulators. Support departmental initiatives to enhance validation practices, streamline validation processes, and leverage advanced tools and technologies to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Basic Qualifications - Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field, and five or more years of relevant experience OR - MA/MS in a quantitative field, and three or more years of related experience OR - PhD in a quantitative field, and less than two years of related experience Preferred Skills/Experience - Master’s or Ph.D. degree in a quantitative discipline with a strong academic record. - Proficiency in Python, SAS, or other analytical programming languages. - Experience working with complex datasets, regression methodologies, and statistical diagnostic tests. - Strong technical writing and communication skills, with attention to detail in documentation and reporting. - Experience leveraging AI tools and agents to support coding, research, and process efficiency. - Strong problem-solving and research skills, with the ability to investigate complex issues, identify root causes, and develop practical business solutions. - Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment, manage multiple priorities, and respond effectively to time-sensitive requests. jobs.title: Finance Rotational Program
jobs.jd: Westlake offers you the potential to enrich your work life and career experience in an entrepreneurial environment. We work together to enhance peoples' lives through our products and presence in the communities in which we operate.​ SUMMARY Graduate Rotational Opportunities at Westlake (GROW) – Finance is a leadership development program for newly graduated students within Westlake Corporation, based in our Houston corporate offices. The GROW Finance program is a 3-year rotational experience designed to expose you to multiple facets of Westlake’s financial operations. You will gain invaluable on‑the‑job experience, a broad understanding of finance from rotations across multiple functional roles, receive professional and leadership training, and contribute to meaningful projects that support a global, integrated producer of chemicals and building products. If you are looking for an opportunity to apply your analytical skills to real‑world business challenges in an environment focused on enhancing lives every day, we encourage you to apply. During your time in the program, you can expect to rotate through different roles in Houston, such as: Corporate Accounting Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Segment / Business Unit Finance Cost Accounting & Manufacturing Finance Treasury / Corporate Finance Internal Audit / Controls & Compliance Tax Investor Relations . DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES May include, but are not limited to, the following You will work in rotational assignments under the guidance of a mentor for each area of focus. Each assignment is designed to develop you as a business leader, strengthen your technical finance and accounting skills, broaden your understanding of finance and the business and empower you to challenge convention and recommend innovative, data‑driven solutions that support value creation and operational excellence. Each rotation is expected to last 12-18 months providing the ability to develop in multiple areas of finance and learn Westlake’s business while allowing sufficient time to make meaningful contributions and impact in each role. Across rotations, you will: Analyze financial performance, prepare management reports and support budgeting and forecasting activities Support month‑end close processes, account reconciliations and preparation of financial statements in accordance with applicable policies and standards Partner with business and operations teams to evaluate investments, projects and cost‑saving initiatives Contribute to continuous improvement of financial processes, controls and systems Participate in ad‑hoc analyses to support strategic decisions, pricing, capital projects and other business initiatives Support independent, objective evaluation of Westlake’s operations, risk management, internal controls and governance Support Westlake’s communication of financial information and strategy to wall street and other public stakeholders Work collaboratively in cross‑functional teams to deliver high‑quality, timely financial insights to leadership As you GROW, you will be: Delivering actionable financial insights and recommendations Identifying and implementing improvements that drive cost savings, margin enhancement and overall efficiency Developing your leadership, communication and stakeholder‑management skills Continuously striving for high performance and adopting a mindset of accountability Doing everything with integrity, safety and compliance at the forefront of your work Adding value for our internal and external customers by helping Westlake invest in our plants, our people and our future Upon successful completion of the program, you may progress into roles such as: Senior Financial Analyst, Senior Accountant, Cost or Plant Finance Analyst, FP&A analyst, or other roles within Westlake’s corporate or segment finance organizations. EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS B.B.A. or M.S. degree in Finance, Accounting, or related business discipline 0–2 years of relevant work experience (including internships or co‑ops) Minimum 3.0 GPA Ability and willingness to rotate across different finance and accounting teams in Houston over 3–5 years Strong analytical, quantitative and problem‑solving skills Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in teams Demonstrated initiative, learning agility and interest in a long‑term career in corporate finance or accounting Working knowledge of Excel and financial / accounting systems; familiarity with data and reporting tools is a plus PHYSICAL DEMANDS While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; stand; walk; use hands to touch, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. jobs.title: (US) Deal Desk Analyst
jobs.jd:
The Deal Desk is a centralized, corporate Revenue Operations function responsible for governing non-standard, high-value commercial deals across PointClickCare. The team partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, and Executive Leadership to ensure pricing, billing, and contractual decisions balance customer flexibility with disciplined financial standards. This role operates as an individual contributor within the Deal Desk, supporting strategic deal reviews and serving as a trusted advisor on complex commercial structures. The Analyst plays a critical role in enabling deal velocity while maintaining consistency, transparency, and governance.  
 
The Deal Desk Analyst supports PointClickCare's Deal Desk by managing the intake, review, and tracking of concession and pricing exception requests. The role ensures every request is accurate, complete, and backed by clear analysis before it reaches approvers, and that decisions are documented and reported consistently. Working under the direction of the Manager, Deal Desk, the Analyst builds pricing workbooks and proposals, maintains Deal Desk data across systems, and produces monthly reporting on concession activity, providing data-driven insights that inform pricing, billing, and contract decisions. This position suits someone with strong Excel and analytical skills, high attention to detail, and an interest in growing into more complex deal structuring work. 
 
Key Responsibilities
Deal Desk Request Intake & Review
Serve as a point of contact for concession and pricing exception requests
Validate request details against internal systems and assess the risks and tradeoffs of each requested concession
Classify each request against the Deal Desk request taxonomy, confirm required approvals, and route to the appropriate approvers
Document decisions, approvals, and rationale so every request has a clear audit trail
Pricing & Deal Analysis
Build pricing models, billing ramps, and revenue forecasts using current pricing and packaging guidelines
Support financial and commercial analysis for non-standard and high-value deals, including the impact of discounts and term changes on MRR and overall deal economics
Convert internal pricing into clean, customer-facing proposals that meet PointClickCare standards
Deal Desk Data, Tracking & Reporting
Maintain Deal Desk approval tracking so reporting stays accurate
Run regular data quality checks and resolve discrepancies across systems and teams
Support monthly Deal Desk reporting on request volume, concession types, approval outcomes, win/loss trends, and more
Sales Support & Cross-Functional Collaboration
Answer rep questions on pricing mechanics, approval requirements, and the Deal Desk intake process
Partner with cross-functional teams to confirm approved terms are set up correctly and accurately reflected in contracts and quotes
Partner with the Manager and fellow Deal Desk Analysts to share knowledge, align on request reviews, and apply standards consistently
Process Improvement & Automation
Help document Deal Desk processes, approval criteria, and the request taxonomy
Identify recurring request patterns and suggest improvements to pricing guidelines and Deal Desk policies
Build and maintain templates, tools, and AI-assisted workflows that reduce manual work and improve turnaround time
Qualifications & Skills
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, analytics, or a related field
1–3 years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, pricing, finance, or a related analytical role
Strong Excel skills (formulas, lookups, pivot tables) and the ability to build basic pricing and financial models
High attention to detail and comfort working with data across multiple systems
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to summarize analysis for Sales and leadership audiences
Ability to manage multiple requests and deadlines in a fast-paced environment
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with CRM tools such as Salesforce
Familiarity with SaaS pricing, discounting, quote-to-cash processes, billing models, and contract structures
Experience using AI tools or automation to streamline analysis and reporting
SaaS and/or healthcare industry experience

jobs.title: Business Analyst
jobs.jd:
Ready to turn sales data into decisions for some of the world’s fastest-growing consumer brands? Join ZURU as a Business Analyst.



Who We Are

ZURU is a reimagination company. We look for categories that have stood still, then we build next-generation products and brands that set the new standard. ZURU Toys is reimagining play. ZURU Edge is reinventing everyday consumer brands. Rhodes Pet Science is reimagining pet science. ZURU Tech is leading the next building revolution.

ZURU started in 2003 with two brothers from New Zealand, and we’re still founder-owned and operated today. Since then we’ve become the world’s second-biggest privately held toy company, and nearly half of all Gen Y and Gen Z households with kids in the US own a ZURU product. Today we’re 5,000 people in 34 offices, selling into more than 150 markets, backed by over 100 acres of fully automated manufacturing. And we’re only getting started.



The Opportunity

ZURU is growing fast, and our Sales team is looking for a Business Analyst who loves numbers and the story behind them. You’ll work across consumer brands like MONDAY Haircare, DAISE, Millie Moon and Rascals + Friends, and toy brands like X-Shot, Bunch of Balloons and Mini Brands, while helping launch new brands to market. You’ll be the analytical engine behind our Key Account team, turning data into decisions and helping shape what ends up on shelf.



The Impact You’ll Make

This is a critical seat at the heart of our commercial team. You’ll be the single source of truth for sales performance across your portfolio, so when the team walks into a retailer meeting, your numbers and insights are what they lean on. You’ll own trade performance reporting, help win range reviews with major retailers and show which promotions actually paid off. Along the way you’ll work with Sales, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain, building the commercial grounding that sets you up for a big career in consumer goods.



What You’ll Do

 - Own weekly, monthly and ad-hoc sales reporting across our key retail customers

 - Build and maintain dashboards that track sell-out, distribution, share of shelf and promotional uplift

 - Track sales against targets, spot risks and opportunities early, and share what you find with the commercial team

 - Measure how promotions performed: work out the return on each one and compare it to forecast and last year

 - Build customer-ready category and brand presentations for range reviews and new listings, using scan data from Quantium, NielsenIQ and Circana

 - Track which products are gaining or losing distribution, and recommend what to do about lines at risk

 - Support new product launches by modelling sales, tracking sell-in and reporting on early sell-out

 - Work with Marketing, Supply Chain and Finance on promo calendars, stock availability, trade spend and monthly commentary



What You’ll Bring

 - Confidence in Excel and PowerPoint: formulas, PivotTables and clean, insight-led slides (we’ll help you sharpen the advanced stuff)

 - A curious, commercial mindset: when you see a number, you want to know the story behind it

 - Sharp attention to detail: you can juggle several deadlines without letting accuracy slip

 - Clear communication: you can explain data simply to people who aren’t analysts

 - A real interest in FMCG, retail or consumer data: no direct experience required



Think you’ve got what it takes? Apply now and tell us your story.





Who thrives at ZURU

This isn’t a 9-to-5. We move fast, think big and set goals most companies would call impossible, then go after them. The people who thrive here are entrepreneurs at heart. They own their work, chase bold ideas and never stop raising the bar.

At ZURU, you drive your career, and we give you the platform to take it as far as you can. There are opportunities here that you won’t find anywhere else, and you’ll be surrounded by talented people who make things happen. We’re a true meritocracy: we reward impact, not tenure.



How we work

Big ideas happen when great people work side by side, so we’re office-first by design. Being together means faster collaboration, sharper decisions and stronger teams, and it’s where the real learning happens. Some flexibility may be available depending on the role, location and business needs, but most roles are office-based.



Want to see what life at ZURU really looks like? Follow @LifeatZURU on Instagram or visit www.zuru.com http://www.zuru.com.



ZURU – Reimagining tomorrow 🚀

Customer Service Analyst II - Supply Chain Replenishment (Onsite: Bentonville, AR) Customer Service Analyst II, Replenishment, is responsible for managing customer inventory to maintain optimal in‑stock levels while adhering to inventory targets and supply constraints. This role monitors and places orders, maintains inventory planning tools, and designs item‑level inventory policies based on demand, lead time, and service expectations. The analyst collaborates cross‑functionally with sales, planning, logistics, and customers to resolve issues, improve order performance, and ensure product availability. They communicate account health through reporting and customer engagement, support onboarding of new business, and drive continuous improvement initiatives by analyzing performance metrics and implementing solutions that enhance efficiency and service delivery. Essential Functions Manage Customer Inventory (40% of time allocated to responsibilities) Monitor, edit, and place orders to maintain agreed in‑stock levels while adhering to inventory targets. Ensure customer orders align with appropriate lead times, stable demand volatility, low percentages of rush orders and cancellations, and Niagara supply constraints to support efficient cost to serve. Monitor and collaborate on metrics not controlled by the Replenishment team but highly influential to their operation. For example, forecast accuracy, on-date delivery, order reschedules, missed pick-ups, appointment availability, percentage of orders scheduled, product availability, and carrier performance. Collaborate with customer to address concerns and initiatives related to ordering tools, data discrepancies, distribution center or store inventory, inventory builds, and changes in ordering or inventory strategies. Support onboarding of new lines of business, including new ship‑to locations and new items within replenishment programs. undefined Collaboration with other departments to resolve critical customer issues (30% of time allocated to responsibilities) Align with customer buyer, merchandizing team, and/or customer supply chain team all tactical and strategic efforts to keep customer inventory healthy and effective. jobs.jd: Job Description: WSJ Newsroom | Data Analyst (September 2026) Title: Data Analyst, Newsroom Analytics The Wall Street Journal is seeking a Data Analyst to join our newsroom data team, reporting to the Senior Manager, Newsroom Analytics. You will work alongside our senior analysts to produce the reports, dashboards, and analyses the newsroom relies on to make editorial, audience, and product decisions every day. This role is a chance to build real analytical range in a fast-moving newsroom environment. You will spend most of your time in SQL, pulling data, building and maintaining dashboards, and helping the newsroom get answers quickly. You will use AI tools to accelerate this work, building lightweight utilities and automations that improve efficiency across the team and free up time for deeper analysis. You will collaborate closely with more senior colleagues as you take on progressively more independent work, from ad hoc analyses to experiment analysis and measurement projects. This position will be based in our New York office. You will: Write SQL to answer questions from newsroom editorial, audience, and product partners, translating requests into clean, well-scoped queries and clearly communicated results. Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports that expand self-serve access to newsroom data. Support deep-dive analyses on major news events, high-priority moments, and shifts in performance. Help keep the reporting stack reliable by troubleshooting data quality issues, tracing problems back to their source, and partnering with data engineering to resolve them. Contribute to A/B tests and experiment analysis in partnership with senior analysts, growing into independent experiment ownership over time. Learn the newsroom's taxonomies, instrumentation, and foundational datasets, and help maintain shared documentation and analytical patterns the team pulls from. You have: 1 to 2 years in data analytics, business intelligence, or a related field, or an equivalent internship and project background. Proficient SQL skills, with experience writing queries against non-trivial datasets. Comfort with a modern BI or dashboarding tool (Looker, Tableau, Mode, or similar). Curiosity and speed in picking up new technical concepts and frameworks, and a track record of getting productive on unfamiliar stacks. Strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to explain data clearly to non-technical partners. Care for accuracy and detail in work the newsroom will act on. Standout candidates will have strengths in one or more of the following: Experience with large-scale data warehouses like BigQuery or Snowflake, or with dbt. Familiarity with Python for analysis, data wrangling, or automation, and comfort maintaining code in Git. Exposure to A/B testing and applied statistics. A background or strong interest in journalism, media, or content, and enthusiasm for driving journalistic outcomes. Comfort using AI/LLM tooling to speed up analytical workflows. jobs.title: Supply Chain Analyst
jobs.jd: About the Company General Matter is enriching uranium in America. Our goal is to design, build, and operate the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services in the United States. Our mission is to restore America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel—fuel that will power AI, advanced manufacturing, critical industries, and the next generation of nuclear reactors. Ultimately, our work will help power national ambitions and enable a high-energy society. We were incubated by Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by top-tier investors. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production. We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency. Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable. About This Role General Matter is building the supply chain that will put American-enriched uranium back into production, and we are looking for a Supply Chain Analyst to keep our teams supplied with everything they need to build. In this role you will support the full range of supply chain functions—purchasing, vendor management, inventory, and data—working shoulder to shoulder with the engineers and operators building mission-critical hardware. You will own problems end to end, from sourcing a custom component to cleaning up the data that tells us what to buy and when. You will primarily operate for a functional area in the business: Software + I&C, Engineering, or Operations. The analyst role works directly with the engineers and operators to turn requirements into orders, ensure all needs are met, and maintain the organizational supply chain. Responsibilities Support procurement and purchasing of components, raw materials, and services for the departments you support, from requisition through delivery. Manage vendor and supplier relationships day to day—placing and expediting orders, tracking performance, and resolving supply issues before they slow the team down. Own category and vendor management for assigned commodities, including qualifying suppliers and negotiating for price, lead time, and availability. Track inventory, demand, and shortages, and give engineering and manufacturing clear visibility into what is clear-to-build. Maintain accurate master data in our ERP/MRP systems and build the reports and analysis the team needs to make fast, informed decisions. Build reports, dashboards, and cost models that drive decisions to capture and communicate the status of the supply chain program. Partner cross-functionally with engineers, operators, and other supply chain team members to identify problems and drive them to resolution with a bias for action. Basic Qualifications Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc). Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals. Ability to perform trade studies and make clear recommendations using first principles and engineering fundamentals even with partial information. Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field. 2–3 years of experience in supply chain, procurement, planning, operations, or a related analytical role (internships included). Preferred Skills and Experience Experience in a fast-paced engineering or highly technical environment, with a resourceful approach to delivering under tight timelines or budget constraints. Hands-on experience with an ERP/MRP system (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Oracle). Strong data management and analysis skills, including advanced proficiency in Excel. Exposure to procurement or purchasing processes, including working with suppliers on lead times, MOQs, and price breaks. Experience in a hardware, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or other highly technical environment. SQL, Python, or BI tools (Power BI, Tableau) experience. Experience buying to nuclear or other quality standards (e.g., NQA-1, 10 CFR Part 21, ISO 9001, AS9100). Additional Requirements: Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary. Equal Opportunity Employer General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. Compensation and Benefits The base salary range for this role is $100,000–$130,000 annually. Compensation bands are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual level and base pay is determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities and internal equity. Please note that the stated salary range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors. In addition to base salary, for full-time hires, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of stock options, and access to medical, vision & dental coverage as well as access to a 401(k) retirement plan.

jobs.jd: JOB TITLE: Analyst, Major League Strategy & Analytics DEPARTMENT: Baseball Strategy FLSA STATUS: Full-time LOCATION: Baltimore, MD REPORTS TO: Assistant General Manager JOB SUMMARY: The Major League Strategy & Analytics Analyst connects Baseball Operations and Research & Development with the Major League coaching staff, using data, models, and scouting information to deliver clear recommendations that coaches and players can deploy. This position reports to the Assistant General Manager and works closely with the Major League Manager and coaching staff, Major League Advance Scouting, Research & Development, Player Development, Professional Scouting, and Major League players. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Primary duties include, but are not limited to, the following : Prepare opponent breakdowns in advance of each series across all pillars of the game, including offense, defense, baserunning, and pitching. Convert analytical processes and models into concise, actionable takeaways that players and coaching staff can use for decision-making and game preparation. Act as the coaching staff’s go-to analytical resource in the clubhouse. Serve as a liaison between the Major League staff and the Baseball Analytics department, ensuring coaching staff questions regarding advanced information are answered in a timely and accurate manner. Analyze and provide feedback to the Analytics department on which analytical tools have the highest impact among staff and players and which tools can be improved upon. Use SQL and R/Python daily to filter through large sets of information in an organized way. Travel with the club and willingness to work non-traditional hours (nights, weekends, holidays) as dictated by Orioles and MLB schedule. WORK LOCATION & TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: Position is based primarily in Baltimore, with travel alongside the Major League team during Spring Training and the regular season. QUALIFICATIONS Completion of Bachelor’s degree, with a preference but not limited to Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, or equivalent. Experience with creating and completing advance materials for a Major League club. Proficiency with SQL, R/Python, and familiarity with Statcast and Hawk-Eye data. Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to collaborate with players and staff members of various backgrounds and responsibilities, and present advanced information in a clear and actionable way. Familiarity with MLB’s in-game and transaction rules. *Applicants with various and/or non-traditional educational background and experience will be considered and are encouraged to apply The anticipated base salary for this role is $60,000 - $80,000 annually depending on experience. jobs.title: PGIM Real Estate – Analyst/Associate, Data Analytics & Governance
jobs.jd: Job Classification: Technology - Data Analytics & Management A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world. We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers! If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today. At PGIM, You Can! What you will do PGIM is seeking an Analyst or Associate, Data Analytics & Governance to join our Global Business Enablement team within Real Estate. This role supports two closely connected priorities: delivering trusted data products and analytics that inform decisions across the real estate investment lifecycle, and putting into practice the data governance that keeps that information accurate, well-defined and reusable. Working alongside other team members, business stakeholders, data stewards and Technology partners, the Analyst/Associate will document business requirements, trace data back to its sources, catalog and define data elements, and build, monitor and report on data quality rules. This is a hands-on role for an early-career professional who enjoys getting into the data, wants to understand how a global real estate investment business operates, and is excited to grow in a modern, AI-enabled data environment. This is a hybrid role (on-site 3 times a week) based in Newark, NJ or New York, NY. What you can expect Data Analytics · Participate in requirements gathering sessions with business stakeholders and document the questions, users, definitions, calculations and acceptance criteria for new data products and reports. · Trace the full data lineage for each new data product, mapping every required data element back to its source system, owner and transformations, and documenting gaps, overlaps and conflicting definitions. · Partner with Technology team members to build and maintain analytical datasets and reports using SQL, Power BI / Fabric and Excel, combining data from multiple internal and external sources. · Work directly with source data to validate assumptions, reconcile results across funds, systems and reports, and investigate variances and anomalies. · Support business testing and validation of new data products by preparing test cases, comparing outputs to source and historical data, and logging and tracking issues to resolution. · Help convert recurring ad-hoc requests into reusable datasets and self-service reports, reducing manual effort and one-off spreadsheet builds. · Prepare and normalize data sets for reporting. · Prepare user guides, data dictionaries and training materials that explain what each data product contains and the questions it can answer. · Support AI use cases across the team by documenting requirements, testing AI-generated outputs for accuracy and reasonableness. Data Governance · Catalog data elements in the firm's data catalog tool (e.g., Microsoft Purview), capturing business definitions, owners, source systems, classifications and lineage. · Maintain the business glossary to keep terminology, calculations and definitions consistent across teams and regions. · Partner with data stewards and subject-matter experts to establish data quality rules (e.g., completeness, validity, consistency, timeliness and accuracy) and encode them as automated, repeatable checks. · Monitor data quality and produce regular data quality metrics, scorecards and trend reporting for stakeholders and governance forums. · Perform root cause analysis of data quality issues, tracing them back to their source, and refer them to the appropriate data stewards for remediation; track issues through to resolution and confirm fixes are made at the source rather than in downstream reports. · Support governance processes, including change management for definitions and datasets, data access requests and the appropriate handling of sensitive data. What you will bring · Bachelor's degree in information systems, finance, economics, real estate, data/analytics or a related field. · 1–3 years of experience in data analysis, business analysis, data governance, data quality or reporting, ideally in commercial real estate, investment/asset management or financial services. · Working proficiency in SQL and advanced Excel; hands-on experience with Power BI or a similar BI tool (Microsoft Fabric a plus) and with semantic models. · Familiarity with data governance concepts, including data catalogs, business glossaries, data lineage, data quality rules and metrics, master data management; experience with Microsoft Purview, Ataccama or similar tools is a plus. · Ability to write clear, well-structured documentation, including business requirements, data definitions, lineage maps and test results. · Comfort working with large, imperfect datasets and reconciling data across multiple systems. · Strong attention to detail, with the instinct to dig into a number that looks wrong and the persistence to find out why. · Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both business and technical colleagues. · Genuine enthusiasm for AI and emerging technologies, demonstrated by hands-on use of current tools and ongoing self-directed learning. · Interest in commercial real estate and investment management; prior exposure is a plus. · A collaborative, curious and organized approach, with an eagerness to learn and grow. *PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply. Note : Prudential is required by state specific laws to include the salary range for this role when hiring a resident in applicable locations. The salary range for this role is from $90,000 to $130,000. Specific pricing for the role may vary within the above range based on many factors including geographic location, candidate experience, and skills. Roles may also be eligible for additional compensation and/or benefits. About PGIM Real Estate With $207.9 billion in gross assets under management and administration ($133.8 billion net),1 PGIM Real Estate provides investors and borrowers access to a range of real estate equity, real estate debt, agriculture, and impact solutions across the risk-return spectrum. PGIM Real Estate is a business of PGIM, the global asset management business of Prudential Financial, Inc. ( NYSE: PRU ). PGIM Real Estate’s risk management approach, execution capabilities and industry insights are backed by a 50-year legacy of investing in commercial real estate, a 140-year history of real estate financing,2 and the local experience of professionals in 32 cities globally. Through its investment, financing, asset management, and talent management approach, PGIM Real Estate engages in practices that strive to ignite positive environmental and social impact, while pursuing activities that seek to strengthen communities around the world. For more information visit pgimrealestate.com . What we offer you: Market competitive base salaries, with a yearly bonus potential at every level. Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, Paid Time Off (PTO), and leave of absences, such as parental and military leave. 401(k) plan with company match (up to 4%). Company-funded pension plan. Wellness Programs including up to $1,600 a year for reimbursement of items purchased to support personal wellbeing needs. Work/Life Resources to help support topics such as parenting, housing, senior care, finances, pets, legal matter
